title: Checkmate!
subtitle: End the game: your first mate-in-one puzzles.
goals: Find mate-in-one with rook and queen

steps.say: Checkmate is how you win: the enemy king is in check, and there is NO way out — no escape square, no block, no capture. Let's learn to spot it.
Watch the difference between a simple check and the real thing.

autoMoves.say: Checkmate! The rook checks along the back rank, and your king guards g7 and h7 — every door is locked. Game over.

hints: The king hides behind his pawns — but they also trap him on the back rank.
Send the rook to the eighth rank.

line.say: The classic back-rank mate! The pawns that sheltered the king sealed his fate.

rejections.say: The seventh rank is nice, but there's no check at all. The king's problem is the EIGHTH rank.

steps.wrongSay: Not mate. Which rank can the king never leave?
steps.successSay: Back-rank mate #1. You'll win real games with exactly this move.

steps.prompt: Queen and king work together — checkmate in one!
hints: Your king already controls d7, e7 and f7 — the king can't step forward.
Put the queen on the back rank, where she covers every remaining square.

line.say: Checkmate! The queen owns the entire back rank, your king covers the escape squares in front — teamwork.

rejections.say: No check — and Black even gets a move. Deliver the blow on the back rank itself.

steps.wrongSay: Not mate — the king wriggles free. Remember: queen attacks the rank, YOUR king guards the escape squares.
steps.successSay: King + queen coordination — the finish of most beginner endgames.

steps.prompt: Two rooks, one ladder. Checkmate in one!
hints: One rook already seals the seventh rank — the king can never step down.
Bring the other rook up to the eighth rank for the final rung.

line.say: The ladder mate! One rook cuts the seventh, the other lands on the eighth. The king had nowhere left to climb.

rejections.say: Check — but by leaving the seventh rank, your rook opened the door: the king escapes to d7. Keep the seventh sealed and mate with the OTHER rook.

steps.wrongSay: Not mate. Keep one rook guarding the seventh rank and strike with the other.
steps.successSay: The two-rook ladder — you'll practice the full climb in a later lesson.

steps.prompt: Careful — one tempting move here is NOT a win, it's a draw! Find the real checkmate.
hints: If the enemy king has no moves but is NOT in check, that's stalemate — a draw! Avoid it.
Mate happens on the back rank, where the check and the trap are the same move.

line.say: Checkmate — check on the rank, king guarding g7 and h7. Clean and final.

rejections.say: STALEMATE! Black isn't in check but has no legal move — the game is instantly drawn. You threw away the win. Always give the cornered king either a check or a square.
Check — but the king steps to g8 and the chase continues. The back rank was the killer.

steps.wrongSay: Watch out for stalemate, and look for the check that covers everything at once.
steps.successSay: You dodged the most painful trap in chess. Stalemate awareness = won games actually won.
